narrative: Material PL3__MEE0F34F exhibits intermittent-high demand across 228 working days, with 74.6% of days showing active consumption averaging 2,303 units and near-zero values on the remainder. On-cycle demand variability is low (CV=0.14), supporting a classical (r,Q) policy, but lead times are highly variable (CV=0.64, range 1.09–5.62 days), making them the primary driver of the 5,245-unit safety stock. The EOQ of ~51,567 units is hard-capped by the 19,632-unit storage limit, yielding a constrained order quantity of 14,386 units that still reduces total annual cost by 84% versus the SAP baseline.
warnings: EOQ (51,567 units) exceeds available storage headroom; order quantity capped at 14,386 units due to max_storage_units=19,631.696 constraint.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Active-day demand is near-normal with low CV (0.14); classical EOQ and ROP calculations are appropriate. Intermittent zeros are structural (schedule gaps) and do not require Croston-type methods.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds strongly: the unconstrained EOQ (51,567) is ~3.6x the storage limit. The capped OQ (14,386) increases replenishment frequency and ordering cost relative to the economic optimum, but total cost remains 84% below the SAP baseline. If storage can be expanded, a larger OQ would further reduce costs.
